_what: Any-tint looks (tools/screen-looks/read-data/tint-look.ts): a person picks one colour, the look keeps only its hue, and every token named here is derived from that hue with a lightness pinned for its role and scheme and a chroma clamped to the role's limit and to what a screen can show. Contrast is therefore a property of the rows, not of the colour picked. `roles` are rows (a token key of the look, a CSS lightness 0-1 and a chroma limit per scheme); a row for a token the look lacks is skipped. A colour with chroma under `neutral_below` has no hue to keep: it is treated as neutral on purpose (chroma 0), never given the browser's accidental hue. The app's own looks name these roles by other token keys (accent-primary, button-primary-bg and its text), so each role has a row for both families; a row for a token the look lacks is skipped. `ground_tokens` are the tokens read, in order, to tell whether a look is light or dark.
